sets.name: 套题 1 — 办公商务场景

part1.text: Good morning, everyone. Welcome to the annual company meeting. Today, we will review the financial results from the past fiscal year and outline our strategic goals for the next twelve months. Please ensure your devices are on silent mode. We will begin with a brief video presentation followed by a Q and A session.
part1.answer: Read at a steady pace (about 130 wpm). Pause slightly at commas. Stress key content words: 'financial results', 'strategic goals', 'Q and A'. Keep a professional, neutral tone throughout.

part1.text: Attention all staff members. The office will be closed this Friday for scheduled maintenance work. All employees are kindly requested to back up their files before leaving on Thursday evening. Regular working hours will resume on Monday morning. Thank you for your cooperation and we apologize for any inconvenience caused.
part1.answer: Stress important information: 'closed this Friday', 'back up their files', 'Thursday evening', 'Monday morning'. Read the final sentence with a slightly warmer, appreciative tone.

part3.background:
Directions: In this part of the test, you will answer three questions based on the survey below.

Situation: Imagine that a North American consulting firm is conducting research on workplace productivity. You have agreed to participate in a telephone interview.

questions.text: How many hours per week do you typically spend in meetings at your workplace?
questions.answer: Sample: 'I typically spend around eight to ten hours per week in meetings. Some of these are daily stand-ups which last about fifteen minutes, while others are longer project reviews that can take one to two hours.'

questions.text: What tools or strategies do you use to stay productive during a busy workday?
questions.answer: Sample: 'I use a combination of time-blocking and a digital to-do list to prioritize tasks. I also try to minimize distractions by setting specific periods for checking emails. Additionally, taking short breaks every ninety minutes helps me maintain focus throughout the day.'

questions.text: If your company introduced a four-day workweek policy, how do you think it would affect your team's performance and morale, and would you personally support it? Please explain in detail.
questions.answer: Sample: 'I believe a four-day workweek could have a significant positive impact on team morale. Employees who feel less burnt-out tend to be more creative and engaged. However, the success of such a policy depends heavily on how tasks are redistributed. Personally, I would support it if clear guidelines were established to ensure clients and deadlines are not affected. For example, my team could work longer hours on the four working days to compensate. Overall, I think the benefits to well-being and retention would outweigh the logistical challenges.'

questions.text: What time does the conference registration begin, and where is the opening keynote being held?
questions.answer: Registration begins at 8:30 AM. The opening keynote, titled 'Innovation in the Digital Age,' is held in Ballroom A at the Grand Pavilion Hotel, starting at 9:00 AM.

questions.text: Where can attendees have lunch, and on which floor is the restaurant located?
questions.answer: Attendees can have lunch at the Terrace Restaurant, which is located on the third floor of the venue. The networking lunch is scheduled at 12:30 PM.

questions.text: A colleague wants to attend the conference but has another commitment in the morning and can only arrive after lunch. Which sessions can she attend, and if she is interested in hands-on learning, which session would you recommend and why?
questions.answer: Your colleague can attend the Workshop Sessions at 2:00 PM, the Closing Remarks and Award Ceremony at 4:00 PM, and the Cocktail Reception at 4:45 PM. For hands-on learning, I would strongly recommend the Workshop Sessions at 2:00 PM. These sessions offer three different tracks, meaning she can choose the topic most relevant to her field. Workshops are typically interactive and practical, which is ideal for someone who prefers learning by doing rather than passive listening. This is the best option for maximizing her time at the conference given her late arrival.

part5.text: Some managers believe that employees are most productive when they are given strict guidelines and close supervision, while others think employees perform better when they are given more autonomy and freedom to manage their own work. Which management style do you think leads to better results, and why? Use specific reasons and examples to support your answer.
part5.answer: Sample answer: 'I believe that giving employees more autonomy generally leads to better results, and I have several reasons for this view. First, autonomy fosters intrinsic motivation. When people have ownership over their work, they are more invested in the outcome and tend to put in greater effort. For example, studies in organizational psychology have shown that self-directed teams often outperform those under strict supervision in creative and problem-solving tasks. Second, micromanagement can create stress and reduce job satisfaction, leading to higher turnover rates, which is costly for companies. That said, I recognize that in certain industries, such as manufacturing or healthcare, strict guidelines are necessary for safety and consistency. In those contexts, a hybrid approach — clear standards with flexibility in execution — tends to work best. Overall, for knowledge-based and creative roles, autonomy with accountability is the most effective model.'

sets.name: 套题 2 — 社区日常生活场景

part1.text: Hello and welcome to the Greenwood Community Center. We are delighted to offer a wide range of programs for residents of all ages this season. From fitness classes and cooking workshops to language courses and art sessions, there is truly something for everyone. Registration is now open and spaces are limited, so we encourage you to sign up early to secure your spot.
part1.answer: Use a warm, welcoming tone. Emphasize phrases like 'wide range of programs' and 'something for everyone'. Slow down slightly at 'spaces are limited' to convey importance. End with a rising, encouraging intonation.

part1.text: The Maplewood Public Library will be hosting its annual book sale this weekend from Saturday through Sunday. Thousands of fiction and non-fiction titles will be available at greatly reduced prices. Proceeds from the sale will go toward purchasing new materials for the children's section. Volunteers are also welcome to help with setup on Friday afternoon.
part1.answer: Stress 'annual book sale', 'greatly reduced prices', and 'children's section'. Maintain a clear, informative tone. Slight emphasis on 'volunteers are welcome' with a positive tone.

part2.answer: Model description: 'The photo shows [setting: a park/market/street]. I can see [number] people who appear to be [doing activity]. The weather looks [sunny/cloudy/rainy]. In the foreground, [describe main subjects]. In the background, there are [buildings/trees/other elements]. The overall atmosphere is [lively/peaceful/busy].'

Model description: 'This picture appears to be taken [indoors/outdoors] in what looks like [location]. Several people are [describing actions]. One person on the [left/right] is [specific action]. The items visible include [objects]. The scene suggests [activity or event].'

part3.background:
Directions: In this part of the test, you will answer three questions based on the survey below.

Situation: Imagine that a local city planning department is conducting a survey about transportation habits. You have agreed to participate in a short telephone interview.

questions.text: How do you usually get to work or school, and how long does your commute take?
questions.answer: Sample: 'I usually take the subway to work. My commute takes about forty minutes each way. I transfer once at Central Station. I generally find it convenient, though it can get quite crowded during rush hour.'

questions.text: What do you think is the biggest problem with public transportation in your city, and what do you think the city should do to improve it?
questions.answer: Sample: 'In my opinion, the biggest issue is overcrowding on the main metro lines during peak hours. I think the city should increase the frequency of trains during those times. Additionally, investing in more bicycle lanes and rental bike stations near transit hubs would encourage people to combine cycling with public transport, which would reduce the overall load on the system.'

questions.text: Some cities are encouraging residents to stop using private cars and switch entirely to public transport or cycling. Do you think this is a realistic and beneficial goal? What challenges might arise, and how could they be addressed?
questions.answer: Sample: 'While the goal of reducing private car use is admirable, I think a complete switch is currently unrealistic for most cities. Many residents rely on cars because public transport does not reach suburban or rural areas effectively. However, it is a beneficial goal worth pursuing gradually. Cities could start by improving the reliability and coverage of public transit, and introducing incentives for switching, such as subsidized transit passes or tax benefits for electric bike purchases. Addressing the concerns of people with mobility issues or those who live far from transit lines is also crucial. With proper investment and planning, a significant reduction in car dependency is achievable within a decade.'

questions.text: If someone is interested in learning a language, what options are available, and on which days are they offered?

questions.text: A friend of mine recently retired and is looking for weekend activities that involve socializing with others. She is interested in both art and community events. Based on the schedule, what would you recommend for her, and how often could she participate in each activity per month?
questions.answer: I would recommend two activities for your retired friend. First, the Watercolor Painting class on Fridays at 3:00 PM — while this is on a weekday, since she is retired, her schedule is flexible. She could attend every week, so approximately four times per month. Second, the Community Book Club held on the second Sunday of each month at 2:00 PM is a perfect fit. It happens once a month and is a wonderful way to socialize with other community members who share an interest in reading and discussion. Both activities are held at the Maplewood Community Center and require prior registration, so she should contact info@maplewoodcc.org to sign up.

part5.text: In recent years, many cities have invested heavily in building new sports facilities, parks, and cultural centers for residents. Some people believe this money would be better spent on improving schools and hospitals. Which type of investment do you think should be a higher priority for city governments, and why? Use specific reasons and examples to support your opinion.
part5.answer: Sample answer: 'I believe that investing in schools and hospitals should take higher priority over sports facilities and cultural centers, and I have two main reasons for this position. First, schools and hospitals address fundamental needs. Quality education and accessible healthcare are basic rights that directly affect people's quality of life and opportunities. For instance, underfunded schools lead to lower literacy rates and reduced economic mobility, while understaffed hospitals result in longer wait times and poorer health outcomes. These are urgent problems that affect everyone. Second, the long-term economic return on investment in education and healthcare is far greater. A well-educated and healthy population is more productive and innovative, which ultimately generates more tax revenue for the city to fund other projects, including cultural centers, in the future. That said, I acknowledge that parks and community centers also play an important role in mental health and social cohesion. A balanced approach — prioritizing essential services while gradually developing community amenities — is probably the most sustainable strategy.'
